newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil court to rule on controversial pay claim.
newsitem.headline: Brazil court to rule on controversial pay claim.

text.p: Brazil's most senior court was due to meet later Wednesday to rule on a pay dispute which could add billions of dollars to the federal government's payroll, a court spokesman said.

The Supreme Federal Tribunal (STF) was due to hold a session at 14:00 local/17:00 GMT to finish setting a case brought by 11 civil servants who want a 28.9 percent pay rise given to the armed forces in 1993, the spokeswoman said.
The civil servants cite a rule that entitles public sector workers to pay rises awarded to state employees in other categories.

Government officials say a victory for the 11 might set a precedent for the entire federal workforce, adding an estimated $7.0 billion to the federal government's payroll spending, which totalled about $42 billion in 1996.
So far, one STF judge has ruled in favor of the civil servants and another has voted against. The court's other eight members are expected to announce their verdicts today.
